paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.
model_annotation: This line chart compares the performance of two methods—ST-ES and Random—for selecting in-context examples, as measured by the metric minFDE₂₀ (lower is better), across different numbers of examples ranging from 0 to 8. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Examples,” is linear and spans from 0 to 8 with tick marks at integer intervals. The y-axis, labeled “minFDE₂₀ (←),” is linear and ranges from 17 to 24, with major gridlines and tick labels at integer values. The ST-ES method is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers: it begins at approximately 21.6 when the number of examples is 0, drops sharply to 18.2 at 1 example, then gradually declines to 17.4 at 4 examples, dips slightly to 17.2 at 6 examples, and ends at 17.4 at 8 examples. The Random method is shown as a solid orange line with circular markers: it starts at 24.0 at 0 examples, decreases to 22.5 at 1 example, then continues a slower decline to 22.0 at 2 examples, fluctuates slightly around 21.8–21.9 through 5 examples, rises marginally to 21.9 at 6 examples, and ends at 21.7 at 8 examples.

model_annotations.English: The line plot illustrates the performance of two methods—“ST-ES” and “Random”—in terms of minimum FDE₂₀ (minFDE₂₀, in meters) as a function of the number of in-context examples, ranging from 0 to 8. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Examples,” is linear and spans integer values from 0 to 8, with major gridlines at each integer. The y-axis, labeled “minFDE₂₀ (←),” is linear and ranges from 17 to 24 meters, with major gridlines at 1-unit intervals. The “ST-ES” method is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers; it begins at approximately 21.6 m at 0 examples, drops sharply to 18.1 m at 1 example, then gradually decreases to 17.3 m at 6 examples before slightly rising to 17.4 m at 8 examples. The “Random” method is shown as a solid orange line with circular markers; it starts at 24.0 m at 0 examples, declines to 22.5 m at 1 example, then stabilizes between 21.7 m and 21.9 m from 2 to 8 examples, showing only minor fluctuations. Both lines exhibit a general downward trend with increasing examples, though ST-ES achieves consistently lower minFDE₂₀ values across all example counts.
